waves.purpose: Native tool/dependency locks versus container boundary
Selected configuration management versus Nix platform adoption

required_now: Reuse native uv0.12.17 with the complete accepted36-package hash lock in a new environment.
Keep native Codex/Claude login and per-client configuration on the destination machine; use reviewed portable recipes, not copied auth stores.
Keep CPU SDK acceptance separate from optional GPU/model/server profiles and host OS prerequisites.
Use explicit native refresh/adoption commands with retained diffs and acceptance evidence; do not silently upgrade the active environment during a session.
optional_later: mise if multi-language tool/artifact bootstrap has concrete value beyond uv; use scoped config, locked install and committed sidecars.
chezmoi only for explicitly selected non-secret file ownership when template/drift management is needed.
One container or Nix environment profile if requirements justify its host dependencies; do not install all three.
future_session_refresh: Check repository revision and the adopted lock fingerprint; unchanged fingerprints should avoid resolution/install/model work.
Refresh source/catalog metadata separately from runtime upgrades. A new release is a review candidate, not authority to replace a working pin.
Create a candidate environment, sync from reviewed hashes, run native metadata/import/CLI checks, then exercise only the authorized model/provider acceptance.
Retain before/after evidence and route changes; MCP/server connection availability and account allowance remain live checks on each destination.
open_boundaries: A same-host fresh-prefix acceptance is not proof of a clean second machine, every OS/architecture or GPU driver compatibility.

SDK hash locking does not make every foundation service, runtime executable, model weight or external data dependency portable. Each adopted profile still needs explicit scoped artifacts and acceptance.

candidates.incremental_value: Adds multi-language tool version management, platform artifact records and task entrypoints if broader native tool bootstrap becomes necessary; current SDK can be reproduced with already adopted uv.
lock_covers: Tool resolutions and backend identity; supported backends record per-platform artifact URLs/checksums.
Version-2 embedded-aube npm sidecars and uv>=0.12.10 PyPI sidecars record transitive CLI dependency graphs and digests.
Native task tools can be included in locking without executing task commands.
lock_omits_and_limits: Application dependencies still need their own native application locks; a tool-manager lock does not replace the SDK hash lock.
Coverage varies by backend. asdf/plugin and source-build lanes have different guarantees; version-only locks remain possible.
Commit generated sidecars with mise.lock. Locked installation can need network and authentication; it is not automatically offline.
CLI dependency graphs do not make lifecycle-script output reproducible. Locked PyPI graphs require a discoverable interpreter and supported wheels; old version-only locks must be explicitly upgraded.
No lock captures provider accounts, MCP connection readiness, host GPU drivers, service data or provider model availability.
Update preview JSON reports version changes only; an empty JSON array does not prove there were no checksum/URL changes.

candidates.incremental_value: Smallest required lane: retain uv0.12.17 and sync the accepted SDK package versions from a hash-bearing requirements lock into a new isolated environment; no new environment manager is necessary.
lock_covers: A complete pinned requirements lock with generated hashes constrains the exact listed package versions and accepted distribution bytes for hash-checking pip sync.
For a true uv project, uv.lock records resolved dependency graph, distribution metadata/hashes and cross-platform/Python marker choices; pyproject.toml remains the dependency intent.
uv sync --locked checks lock freshness; uv pip sync makes the selected environment match the supplied complete requirements set.
lock_omits_and_limits: requirements.txt compiled for one environment is not automatically a universal project lock; target Python/platform and accepted wheel coverage must be stated.
An all-pinned 36-package environment inventory is an observed resolved SDK, not a declaration that all its versions are latest.
Hashes do not authenticate publishers independently or approve license/vulnerability status. Source builds have additional inputs; --no-build can require wheel-only acceptance.
Neither uv.lock nor requirements hashes install host GPU drivers, system services, model weights or provider credentials. A Python interpreter/build pin is separate.

uv --frozen skips freshness checks; it is not interchangeable with --locked. Project sync removes extraneous packages by default, so adopt into a new prefix instead of modifying the active worker SDK.
